text:
sam: FYI seeing intermittent 502s from inference-edge-sg since ~03:20 UTC. Errors correlate with GPU pool autoscale events. :eyes:

sam: Symptoms — headless svc (`headless-modelpool.inference.svc`) resolves, but client pods get connection errors and retries. `curl` to pod IPs times out or returns 502s.

sam: Quick grep of EndpointSlice shows endpoints present but some entries have `nodeName` only, no `targetRef` (pods got evicted during scale):
```
$ kubectl get endpointslice -n inference headless-modelpool -o yaml | sed -n '1,40p'
addresses:
  - 10.40.22.11
  - 10.40.22.12
endpoints:
  - nodeName: ip-10-40-22-11.ap-sg
    conditions: {ready: true}
  - nodeName: ip-10-40-22-12.ap-sg
    conditions: {ready: true}
```

sam: Also seeing lots of conntrack entries piling up on the affected nodes: `ESTABLISHED` and a bunch of `SYN_RECV` to backend ports.

anya: Did kube-proxy recently roll? Any crashloops?

sam: kube-proxy logs show repeated iptables sync warnings and `failed to ensure service` for the headless svc during the autoscale window. No crashloop though.

miguel: This smells like kube-proxy iptables sync + conntrack race when pods move off nodes. We've seen stale conntrack keeping NAT translations and clients hitting old node IPs. Are we on iptables mode or ipvs?

sam: iptables mode for these clusters (edge region).

elaine: Node-local-dns is in place, but this looks below DNS. Could be kube-proxy leaving rules in a transient state and endpointslice not reflecting targetRef fast enough after eviction.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaled up nodegroup gpu-edge-sg by 3 nodes at 03:18:52 UTC (reason: pending pods).

ops-oncall: Plan: (1) drain one affected node, (2) restart kube-proxy on the other two nodes, (3) flush conntrack on those nodes, (4) observe for 5m. Anyone object? :+1:

anya: +1 do it. Also capture `iptables-save` before restart so we can diff.

sam: Doing on ip-10-40-22-11 now — restarted kube-proxy, flushed conntrack (`sudo conntrack -F`), restarted nginx sidecars on a few client pods.

miguel: Adding a note — when restarting kube-proxy prefer systemd restart rather than delete pod (we had a bug where CNI rules were briefly re-applied).

sam: After restarts/flushes traffic looks stable, 502s dropped to zero in the last 3m. Node with drain had zero active endpoints for ~30s during eviction which probably exposed the race.

elaine: Can we add an alert for (endpointslice address count != endpoint targetRef count) AND conntrack spikes on kube-proxy nodes? That should catch this earlier.

ops-oncall: Filed INFRA-1218 to add endpoint/targetRef divergence alert, and INFRA-1219 for conntrack rate anomaly.

sam: Thanks all. Follow-up: evaluate ipvs mode and whether kube-proxy sync periods need tuning for GPU autoscale churn. :pray:

miguel: Also worth adding a post-scale hook to wait for EndpointSlice `targetRef` stabilization before routing traffic to new nodes.

ops-oncall: Closing thread — reopening if we see recurrence.
